question.text: Per the current NISM XIX-A workbook, what is the maximum number of investors permitted per scheme of an AIF (other than angel funds)?

answer.text: Not more than 1,000 investors per scheme
No upper limit on the number of investors per scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM XIX-A workbook states that an AIF scheme may have not more than 1,000 investors. Angel funds are governed by separate rules in the same workbook — they shall not launch schemes for soliciting funds/making investments and must have at least five accredited investors before the first close. The earlier framing of "200 investors per angel fund scheme" should not be used as a numeric key without a current source citation. The Trap: 500 is an older or unrelated cap; 200 reflects the legacy angel-fund framing rather than the general AIF scheme cap. "No upper limit" contradicts the workbook. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XIX-A is the primary source for AIF scheme structural caps; X-B and III-C cross-reference these caps when advising clients or assessing fund-house compliance.
